# Tensorial and Low-Rank Representations

Also called: Tensor Factorization, Tensor Decomposition Radiance Fields

## Overview
Tensorial and Low-Rank Representations address the high memory consumption and overfitting issues inherent in dense [voxel-based radiance fields](#11470-voxel-based-radiance-fields.md) by modeling the scene as a factorized 4D tensor [3026-tensorf.md]. Unlike [Direct Voxel Grid Optimization](4694-direct-voxel-grid-optimization.md), which stores independent features per voxel, this family exploits the low-rank structure of geometry and appearance to correlate the entire field, reducing space complexity from $O(n^3)$ to $O(n)$ or $O(n^2)$ [G]. It sets itself apart from [NeRF](4972-neural-radiance-fields.md) by replacing multi-layer perceptrons (MLPs) with compact vector and matrix factors, enabling significantly faster reconstruction and smaller model sizes [3026-tensorf.md].

## Shared principles
All methods in this family represent the radiance field as a low-rank tensor [decomposition](#7254-decomposition.md), typically using Canonical Polyadic (CP) or Vector-Matrix (VM) formats [3026-tensorf.md]. The core mechanism replaces the implicit function of an MLP or the dense grid of a voxel field with a set of global mode vectors and matrices [3026-tensorf.md].

For a 4D radiance field $\mathcal{F}(x, y, z, \theta)$, where $(x,y,z)$ are spatial coordinates and $\theta$ represents view-dependent parameters, the field is approximated by a sum of rank-1 components [3026-tensorf.md]. In the [Vector-Matrix (VM) decomposition](#3452-vector-matrix-vm-decomposition.md), the density $\sigma$ and appearance features $\mathbf{c}$ are computed by interpolating mode vectors and matrices [3026-tensorf.md]. For a component $r$, the density contribution is a sum of terms like $\mathbf{v}_X(x) \cdot \mathbf{M}_{YZ}(y,z)$, where $\mathbf{v}$ is a vector and $\mathbf{M}$ is a matrix [3026-tensorf.md]. This structure allows for efficient trilinear interpolation and differentiable rendering [3026-tensorf.md].

The training process typically employs a coarse-to-fine strategy [3453-tensorf-reconstruction-optimization.md]. Optimization begins at a low resolution $N_0^3$ (e.g., $128^3$) and upsamples the tensor factors at specific iteration steps (e.g., 2000, 3000, 4000) using linear interpolation for vectors and [bilinear interpolation](#858-bilinear-interpolation.md) for matrices [3453-tensorf-reconstruction-optimization.md]. Regularization is critical to prevent overfitting; L1 norm loss on factors encourages sparsity, while Total Variation (TV) loss promotes smoothness, particularly for datasets with few views or imperfect capture [3453-tensorf-reconstruction-optimization.md].

## Subtopics

### [TensoRF](3026-tensorf.md)
Models the radiance field as a factorized 4D tensor using CP or VM decomposition. It sets itself apart from implicit MLPs and sparse voxels by achieving superior memory efficiency through global mode vectors and matrices. Choose it for fast reconstruction and compact storage.

### [TensoRF Reconstruction Optimization](3453-tensorf-reconstruction-optimization.md)
The iterative gradient-based procedure to fit tensorial fields to multi-view images. It sets itself apart by enforcing structural regularization (L1/TV) on factors and using dynamic coarse-to-fine upsampling. Choose it for the standard [training loop](#4290-training-loop.md).

### [Joint Optimization of Camera Pose and Decomposed Low-Rank Tensorial Radiance Fields](11498-joint-optimization-of-camera-pose-and-decomposed-low-rank-te.md)
Jointly refines camera poses and scene geometry using only 2D image supervision. It sets itself apart by integrating spectral filtering to avoid local optima caused by the lack of spectral bias in voxels. Choose it when camera poses are unknown.

### [Strivec Fast Variant](11867-strivec-fast-variant.md)
A computationally optimized configuration of the [Strivec](#11863-strivec.md) method. It sets itself apart by reducing multi-scale levels and top-k candidates during ray sampling for faster training and inference. Choose it when speed is prioritized over maximum detail capture.

### [HexPlane](12007-hexplane.md)
An explicit representation for dynamic 3D scenes that decomposes a 4D [spacetime](#7334-spacetime.md) grid into six learned feature planes. It sets itself apart by pairing [spatial planes](#9808-spatial-planes.md) with spatio-temporal planes to capture entangled space-time dynamics. Choose it for dynamic novel view synthesis.

### [Few TensoRF](12481-few-tensorf.md)
A 3D reconstruction framework combining tensor-based representation with [frequency-driven regularization](#6130-frequency-regularization.md). It sets itself apart by applying a dynamic frequency mask to prioritize low-frequency information in early training stages. Choose it for few-shot reconstruction.

### [LOD Generation](13123-lod-generation.md)
Creates multiple levels of detail from a trained finest-resolution radiance field model. It sets itself apart by leveraging the compressibility of rank-residual models and merging blocks with adapted deferred MLPs. Choose it for efficient rendering of large composed scenes.

## Background
The concept of tensor decomposition for radiance fields was introduced by [TensoRF](3026-tensorf.md), which demonstrated that radiance fields exhibit low-rank structures in both geometry and appearance. Prior methods like [NeRF](4972-neural-radiance-fields.md) relied on MLPs, which are memory-efficient but slow to train, while voxel-based methods like [Direct Voxel Grid Optimization](4694-direct-voxel-grid-optimization.md) were fast but memory-intensive [G]. TensoRF bridges this gap by using tensor factorization to achieve both speed and compactness [3026-tensorf.md]. The joint optimization variant addresses the instability of optimizing poses with [voxel-based representations](#10852-voxel-based-representation.md) by leveraging the spectral bias and smoothness properties of the tensor factors [11498-joint-optimization-of-camera-pose-and-decomposed-low-rank-te.md].
